expectations.text: Report identifies truncate was named shorten instead
expectations.evidence: Report states under Deviations: '1. truncate renamed to shorten (string_utils.py:4): The plan specifies truncate(text, max_length, suffix="...") but the implementation uses shorten(text, max_len, ellipsis="..."). The comment in the code explicitly notes this.'

expectations.text: Report identifies word_count was named count_words instead
expectations.evidence: Report states: '2. word_count renamed to count_words (string_utils.py:20): The plan specifies word_count(text) but the implementation uses count_words(text). The comment in the code explicitly notes this.'

expectations.text: Report identifies reverse_words as an unplanned addition not in the plan
expectations.evidence: Report states: '3. Unplanned function reverse_words added (string_utils.py:34-36): The plan does not include a reverse_words function, but one was added. The comment notes: "Deviation: unplanned function not in the plan."'

expectations.text: Report confirms tests pass despite naming deviations
expectations.evidence: Report shows 'Tests pass: make test - 7/7 tests passed (100%)' and lists all 7 tests as PASSED including test_shorten, test_count_words, test_reverse_words.

expectations.text: Report notes parameter naming differences (max_length→max_len, suffix→ellipsis)
expectations.evidence: Report states: 'the implementation uses shorten(text, max_len, ellipsis="..."). Both the function name and parameter names differ.' And in Recommendations: 'Rename parameters in truncate: max_len → max_length and ellipsis → suffix to match the plan signature exactly.'

expectations.text: Report distinguishes between deviations (naming) and completeness (functionality works)
expectations.evidence: Report summary states: 'The implementation is functionally correct and all tests pass. However, there are three notable deviations from the plan: truncate was renamed to shorten (with parameter renames), word_count was renamed to count_words, and an unplanned reverse_words function was added.' Summary table shows 'Automated tests pass: PASS (7/7)' while flagging naming deviations separately.

claims.claim: Any callers expecting truncate or word_count per the plan would fail at runtime
claims.evidence: Report explicitly flags this: 'API contract mismatch: Any callers expecting truncate(text, max_length, suffix="...") or word_count(text) per the plan would fail at runtime.'
Report states 'The behavior is functionally correct (shorten("Hello World", 8) returns "Hello...")' and all 7 tests pass.

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions, evals look solid. Assertions correctly distinguish naming deviations from functional correctness, which is the key discriminating factor in this scenario.
